ordering_rationale: All 91 immutable contracts are allocated exactly once across operation-centered theories under the sole fixed parent profile; all owned contexts are empty. Array order prioritizes normalization, the intertwined tree executor, small overlap cases and independent read-only observations before their consumers. Required imports commit to retained semantic result interfaces, not implementation calls or scheduling preferences. In particular queries have no update dependency; primitive tree operations share a physical theory because rotation removes promoted entries and removal rotates/prunes. Restricted pair overlap and singleton insertion need no general correspondence theorem; canonical measure and canonical uniqueness stay with their general consumers. Primitive Interval_Cutting is ready independently and is prioritized after the existing four independent foundations. Normalization -> canonical algebra -> Cutting_Normalization and primitive cutting -> Cutting_Normalization are committed composition interfaces. Primitive cutting and normalization -> measure feed Repeated_Cutting, which no longer waits for normalization-interaction equalities; components use normalization but do not impose a reverse graph-theory dependency. Atomic state updates use tree execution; traces use atomic updates and observations. A larger merge/chop monolith and separate mutually dependent rotation/removal files were rejected. Collaboration groups and reciprocal suggestions remain advisory and cannot authorize cross-theory premises; promoting any new reuse requires revisiting the frozen imports. No proof DAG or exact helper statements are prescribed. Pre-freeze review separates five composition contracts from eleven primitive cutting contracts. This semantic interface change adds one theory, not a proof route. Canonical preservation concerns assumed canonical inputs and does not require general normalized-output correspondence. The remaining measure prerequisite is deliberate; no further split is justified by this review.
